To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the constitutive activation of cytokinin signaling by a phosphomimetic mutant of Arabidopsis ARR1 results in a constitutive cytokininsensitive phenotype.

constitutive activation of the cytokinin signal transduction pathway in Arabidopsis thaliana by ectopic expression of a phosphomimetic form of the response regulator 1 protein results in a cytokinin-like phenotype, and that this constitutively activated form of the response pathway is sufficient to induce the expression of cytokinin-responsive genes and cytokinin-mediated developmental changes.

the constitutively active phosphomimic form of the cytokinin response regulator ARR1 promotes cytokinin responses and that the phosphomimetic form of ARR1 is a constitutive activator of cytokinin responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and physiological characterization of the phosphomic mutant ARR1D94.
the molecular mechanisms of cytokinin signaling, and the data presented here will be of interest for those working in the field of plant hormone signaling.
the role of the phosphomicic residue in RRB1 in cytokinin signaling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ARR1 protein, in the context of the plant, is a bona fide cytokinin response activators.
the phosphomimetic mutant ARR1D94 is an active cytokinin response regulator.
overexpression of the phosphomimidic mutant of Arabidopsis RRC 1 promotes a cytokinin-like response, and that the phosphomimidate residue in RRBs plays an essential role in cytokinin signaling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the D94E substitution in the ARR1 receiver domain is a strong positive regulator of cytokinin responses, and this is the first evidence that the phosphorylation state of the RRB receiver domain is a critical regulator of cytokinin sensitivity.

the D94E substitution of ARR1D94 confers a constitutive and enhanced cytokinin signaling response phenotype, and this phosphomimic mutation of RRBs can be used to study the role of RRBs as cytokinin response regulators in Arabidopsis.
the constitutive activity of the ARR1D940E protein is responsible for the cytokinin-like phenotype in the overexpressing plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the D94 residue is essential to the regulation of the activity of RRBs and thus to the regulation of cytokinin responses.
the D94E substitution in the RRB1 receiver domain is not a phosphomimetic mutation but rather a gain-of-function mutation that promotes a cytokinin hypersensitive phenotype.

, while the D94E mutation in ARR1 is a constitutive activator of cytokinin signaling, the wild-type ARR1 protein can still be activated in response to cytokinins, and this activation leads to a more restricted set of cytokinin responses.
